item.title: There goes my Hero
item.description: Professional racing driver Ollie Millroy thanks competitor Loek Hartog for saving his life after getting into a fiery crash over the weekend in China. Millroy says he'd be dead if Hartog hadn't jumped out of his car to pull him out of his burning car. "I am still alive tonight, entirely thanks to one man. Loek Hartog stopped instantly with no flag marshalls or fire crews in sight, and risked his own life to get me out of the car." "I don’t remember anything between 30 seconds before the crash and 1 hour after it, but I will remember his incredible act of bravery for the rest of my life..." "I’m laying here tonight with 5 broken ribs, broken collar bone, broken hand and finger and a bruised lung, but it could have been much worse." "Thank you Loek. I owe you my life for your selfless act today." Quote from Hartog: Hartog wrote on social media that Millroy had nothing to thank him for, saying he wished anyone else in his position had done the same. "I wish to live in a world where this would not be considered as bravery but as instinct of others too," Hartog wrote. "I am so thankful to have been right at the place I needed to be in space and time." More: https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-09-07/ollie-millroy-loek-hartog-china-gt-flaming-crash/107122520

item.description: $12.99 for a 12 pack of Sprite in North San Diego is wild. That is basically $1.08 per can before tax or CRV. And yeah, the digital coupon drops it to $4.99, but only if you buy 5 or more. That is the part that annoys me. The “normal” price is insane, then suddenly the store can knock $8 off if you agree to buy a small warehouse worth of soda. So apparently the real price is somewhere between “reasonable” and “absolutely not,” depending on whether you are willing to stockpile it. This is why grocery shopping feels like a game now. Regular price. Member price. Digital coupon. Buy 5. Mix and match. Scan the app. Meanwhile I just wanted one case of Sprite.

item.title: GovBrief Today #586
item.description: A Border Patrol analyst in Spokane read a stranger's bank activity, and a Montana trooper found a reason to pull him over. Nobody knows how a federal agent in Washington and a state trooper in Montana came to be talking about one black Chevy on Interstate 90, because the government won't say. We know it happened only because the paperwork surfaced in his court case. The analyst's memo says he saw "financial activity patterns" in federal databases and put the car out as a lookout. On bodycam, the trooper told the driver it was "nothing major," just a plate cover. The Spokane unit is called the Predictive Intelligence Targeting Team, and true to its name, it exists to predict whether you might be doing something illegal. Customs and Border Protection will not say what financial records it reads, whether a warrant is involved, or how many of its 20 sectors participate. In Texas the same program had a deputy search a driver's truck on a lane-drift stop and find nothing. That driver was never charged. item.title: Pure Cinema: Sharing My Letterboxd Likes Day 109
item.description: A pair of dimwitted criminals aim to join the notorious Axe Gang in this wuxia/musical/comedy/cartoon mashup. Written and directed by Stephen Chow (SHAOLIN SOCCER), it’s impossible to cleanly categorize this film. There are dance numbers, breathtaking martial arts sequences, top-tier physical and visual comedy, and chases right out of a Roadrunner short. It’s a cinematic gumbo of styles and influences, and it’s a joy to watch. KUNG FU HUSTLE is available to rent or buy on all the standard apps.
